extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying to Alzheimer’s Research UK grant schemes (dementia/Alzheimer's researchers, clinicians, early-career researchers)
extracted.subtask_short: applying to Alzheimer's Research UK grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/assessment criteria for applying to the range of grant schemes run by Alzheimer’s Research UK, including the funder's remit, priority topics, emphasis on translational potential, scheme-specific eligibility, and the basis on which awards are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit to Alzheimer's Research UK remit
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must fall within Alzheimer’s Research UK’s remit which covers biomedical research in Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an eligibility gate: applications outside biomedical research in Alzheimer’s and other dementias will not be considered. Ensure the proposed work clearly maps to the funder's remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funded research topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Alzheimer’s Research UK funds research into treatment, diagnosis and prevention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should address one or more of these topic areas. Emphasising relevance to treatment, diagnostic tools, or preventive strategies aligns with funding priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translational potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Of particular importance is research which has translational potential to benefit people with or at risk of dementia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translational potential includes basic preclinical as well as clinical research. Applicants should state how the project could lead to outcomes that benefit patients or at-risk populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion: care or service delivery research
rubrics_metrics.description: This includes basic preclinical as well as clinical research, but not care or service delivery research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care/service-delivery projects are explicitly out of scope for ARUK's biomedical remit; applicants in those areas should seek alternative funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant applications undergo a rigorous review process and are awarded on the basis of scientific merit in relation to Alzheimer's Research UK’s remit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals will be assessed for quality of science, rationale, methods, feasibility, and potential impact relative to the funder's remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for the scheme applied for
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards are made on the basis of ... suitability for the scheme applied for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each scheme has specific aims and eligibility; applicants must select the scheme that matches their career stage, project scale, and objectives. Mismatching scheme and proposal may lead to rejection regardless of scientific merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are awarded ... and open competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding decisions are competitive; applicants should assume proposals will be evaluated against other high-quality submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous review process (procedural standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant applications undergo a rigorous review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect formal review procedures (peer review/committee) and prepare application materials to meet review expectations (clear aims, robust methods, appropriate CVs/track record).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Clinical Fellowship – scheme eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced Clinical Fellowship: For clinicians who’ve delivered previous dementia research projects and have clear plans to establish their own research programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted at clinician-researchers with prior dementia research experience and a plan to lead an independent programme; include evidence of prior projects and a credible programme plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Career Researcher Bridge Fund – scheme aim
rubrics_metrics.description: Early Career Researcher Bridge Fund: This scheme aims to enable the retention of early career researchers in dementia research or to address particular pinch points in their career path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to prevent loss of talent at career transitions; applications should demonstrate how funding will retain the researcher or address a defined career pinch point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspire Fund – public engagement grant – scheme aim
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspire Fund – public engagement grant: The Inspire Fund provides funding for projects that engage the public with the topic of brain health and reducing the risk of dementia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on public engagement and awareness-raising around brain health and dementia risk reduction; include plans for audience engagement and measurable outreach outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Race Against Dementia Fellowship – scheme aim
rubrics_metrics.description: Race Against Dementia Fellowship: For early-career scientists in their pursuit of innovative solutions to the big questions in dementia research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aimed at early-career researchers pursuing high-innovation projects; emphasize novelty and potential to address major dementia research questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot Projects – scheme aim
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot Projects: Meant for novel research ideas that, if successful, would lead to a Major project or programme application to Alzheimer’s Research UK or other funding body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed as seed funding to generate preliminary data or proof-of-concept; applications should describe how success would enable a subsequent larger application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major Projects – scheme aim
rubrics_metrics.description: Major Projects: Meant for intermediate to large-scale research projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for larger-scale programmes; proposals should demonstrate capacity for managing multi-year, multi-investigator projects and deliver substantial outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior Research Fellowship – scheme eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior Research Fellowship: For PhD-qualified researchers in transition to lead independent groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted at researchers moving into independent group leadership; include evidence of readiness to lead and plans for establishing a research group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Fellowship – scheme eligibility (non-clinical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Fellowship: For PhD-qualified non-clinical researchers who have clear plans to establish their own research niche.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aimed at non-clinical PhD holders seeking to develop an independent niche; detail niche area, feasible aims, and career development plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctoral Clinical Fellowships – scheme eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctoral Clinical Fellowships: For clinically qualified applicants wishing to develop a career that combines dementia research and professional practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For clinicians pursuing doctoral training that links research with clinical practice; applications should articulate integration of research and professional development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheme selection and career-stage alignment (implicit criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The listed variety of schemes (career development, clinical, projects, fellowships, pilot/major projects, events-based grants) implies selection based on career stage, project scale and purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must align their career stage and project goals with the most appropriate scheme (e.g., early-career support vs major project funding vs public engagement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural migration note
rubrics_metrics.description: Alzheimer’s Research UK has now migrated to Flexigrant and has ceased to use GrantTracker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should use the current application system (Flexigrant) and follow any updated submission procedures; do not rely on older GrantTracker instructions.
